mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE increases by > 0.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of instances when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases by > 2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases by > 300k and UNRATE decreases by > 0.2%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST increases for two consecutive months, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected drop in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a potential deflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market participants anticipate a slowdown in consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive but below 1% for two consecutive quarters, and retail sales (RSAFS) simultaneously decline by more than 1% in a month, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% for 2 quarters & RSAFS decreases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth is < 1% for two quarters and RSAFS decreases by > 1%, this hypothesis is rejected.
